text: When an adult's office blood pressure reading is 130/80 mm Hg or higher and the patient has no symptoms, repeat the measurement after five minutes of seated rest. If the repeat reading is still elevated, schedule a nurse blood pressure check within four weeks and offer a home blood pressure monitor. Do not start medication on a single office reading.

Send an adult for same-day evaluation when the systolic reading is 180 mm Hg or higher or the diastolic reading is 120 mm Hg or higher together with chest pain, shortness of breath, new confusion or vision changes. Without these symptoms, repeat the reading and contact the on-call clinician before the patient leaves.

Ask patients using a home monitor to take two readings one minute apart, morning and evening, for seven days before the follow-up visit. Average the readings, leaving out the first day, and record the average in the chart.

After a positive fecal immunochemical test, refer the patient for diagnostic colonoscopy and aim to complete it within 60 days of the result. Do not repeat the stool test to confirm a positive result. Record the referral date and track it on the screening registry.
After a positive FIT, refer the patient for diagnostic colonoscopy, which should take place within 90 days. A repeat FIT may be offered if the patient declines colonoscopy.

Offer average-risk adults aged 45 to 75 either a fecal immunochemical test every year or a colonoscopy every ten years. Patients with a first-degree relative diagnosed before age 60 follow the increased-risk pathway instead.
Review the written asthma action plan with adult patients at least once a year, and at every visit after an emergency department attendance for asthma.
Review the written asthma action plan with the child and caregiver every six months, and give an updated copy to the school nurse at the start of each school year.
Check inhaler technique at every asthma review by asking the patient to demonstrate it. Children under five use a spacer with a face mask.

Measure HbA1c every three months in adults whose treatment changed or whose last result was above their individual target. When the result is at target and treatment is stable, measure it every six months.

Every adult with diabetes has a foot examination at least once a year, including monofilament testing and a pulse check. Refer to podiatry within two weeks if there is an ulcer or a new loss of protective sensation.
Refer adults with diabetes for retinal screening at the diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and then every year. Patients with two consecutive normal screens may move to every two years.
Patients approved for home INR self-testing check their INR once a week for the first month and then every two weeks, phoning each result to the anticoagulation clinic on the day of the test.

Patients taking warfarin who attend the anticoagulation clinic have their INR checked at every clinic visit. The clinic pharmacist sets the interval between visits, and it is never longer than twelve weeks.
Ask every adult about tobacco use at each visit, advise users to quit, and offer both behavioural support and medication to help them stop. Record the offer and the response in the chart.
Refer patients who want to quit to the Larkspur quit program, which offers six weekly counselling sessions. Nicotine replacement can start on the quit date.
Children who are behind on routine vaccines follow the catch-up schedule held by the immunization nurse. Do not restart a vaccine series because of a delay; continue from the last recorded dose.
Offer influenza vaccine to every adult each autumn, starting when the clinic receives the season's supply. Pregnant patients may receive it in any trimester.
Any infant younger than 28 days with a temperature of 38.0 C or higher is sent for same-day emergency evaluation. Do not give fever-reducing medicine before the infant is assessed.
A potassium result above 6.0 mmol/L is a critical value. The lab phones the ordering clinician, who contacts the patient the same day and documents the plan within two hours of the call.
The ordering clinician reviews non-urgent abnormal results within three working days, and the patient is told the result and the plan within seven working days.
Screen adults for depression with the PHQ-2 at the annual visit. A positive PHQ-2 is followed by a PHQ-9 at the same visit.
Screen adolescents aged 12 to 17 for depression with the PHQ-A at the annual visit. The clinician reviews a positive result at the same visit.

Ask adults aged 65 and older at each annual visit whether they have fallen in the past year. Offer patients who have fallen, or who report unsteadiness, a gait and balance assessment and a referral to the strength and balance class.
